categories.description: Research on compact, efficient representations of game worlds using latent spaces, including variational autoencoders, diffusion models, and neural radiance fields tailored for 3D environments.
Methods for algorithmically generating game assets, levels, narratives, and rulesets, ranging from grammar-based systems to deep learning-driven generative models.
Techniques enabling agents or systems to simulate future states, reason about consequences, and plan actions within a modeled world, often involving differentiable physics or learned dynamics.
Systems that allow users to guide, edit, or constrain world generation in real-time through natural language, sketches, or other interfaces, emphasizing human-in-the-loop design.
Standardized datasets, tasks, and quantitative/qualitative measures used to assess the quality, diversity, realism, and utility of generated or simulated game worlds.

Specialized world modeling approaches tailored to specific game genres, addressing requirements such as low-latency control in action games, stateful persistence in adventure games, and role fidelity in role-playing games.
Applications of game world modeling techniques to external domains such as autonomous driving, robotics, and social simulacra, leveraging shared foundations in video generation and simulation.
